routes.description: Establish that evolutionary science is logically compatible with theistic guidance and that naturalism combined with evolution creates an undefeated reliability defeater.
routes.successCriteria: Show both that evolutionary mechanisms do not entail absence of divine guidance and that accepting naturalism plus evolution rationally undercuts trust in the cognition producing that conjunction.

motionBridge.description: Evolutionary science and theistic religion are compatible, while naturalism plus evolution undercuts rational trust in cognition.

centralBridges.description: Random mutation and natural selection, scientifically understood, do not entail that evolution is unguided or unintended.
Given naturalism and evolution, reliable belief content is improbable because selection directly rewards adaptive physiology and behavior rather than truth.
A defeater for cognitive reliability propagates to naturalism and evolution themselves, making their conjunction rationally self-defeating.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Cellular complexity and Behe's argument provide at least provisional evidential support for guided evolution.
Methodological restriction within scientific practice is distinct from assuming metaphysical naturalism.

routes.description: Concede bare logical compatibility while arguing that guided evolution lacks evidential support and that evolution can produce corrigible truth-tracking cognitive systems without divine design.
routes.successCriteria: Show that compatibility alone gives no reason to prefer theistic guidance over gratuitous alternatives, defend naturalistic scientific practice, and defeat the claimed low probability of reliable cognition under evolution.

motionBridge.description: Bare compatibility does not support theistic guidance, and naturalistic evolution does not undercut rational trust in cognition.

centralBridges.description: Theistic guidance is logically possible but evidentially gratuitous relative to naturalistic evolutionary explanation.
Naturalistic assumptions appropriately govern reputable empirical and legal explanation without requiring a separate proof of metaphysical naturalism in each inquiry.
Selection and cultural-scientific correction can build syntactic systems whose continued functioning depends on tracking truth.

subsidiaryBridges.description: The scientific response and incentive structure undermine reliance on Behe's claims of irreducible complexity.
Measurement, prostheses, language, and scientific methods identify and correct cognitive shortcomings.

sections.title: Logical compatibility and evidential significance
sections.rationale: The opening dispute distinguishes bare consistency between Darwinism and divine guidance from whether that consistency supplies evidential support for theism.

proMoves.speaker: Alvin Plantinga
proMoves.proposition: Darwinian evolution is compatible with divine guidance because God could cause or preserve the mutations and populations needed for intended creatures, while biological randomness does not mean uncaused or unintended.

sourceSpan.excerpt: God could have caused the right mutations to arise at the right time... Darwinism is entirely compatible with God's guiding, orchestrating, and overseeing the whole process.

proMoves.attributionBasis: The span occurs within Plantinga's uninterrupted opening presentation, introduced by the moderator.

response.rationale: This is the first selected constructive statement of the compatibility route and has no earlier selected target.

precisionFindings.rationale: Plantinga distinguishes Darwinism, unguided evolution, causal randomness, and metaphysical naturalism, and explicitly limits the conclusion to compatibility.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The modal compatibility claim is strongly supported by the described possible mechanism, though 'entirely compatible' compresses questions about the full theological account.

charity.alternative: Evolutionary theory itself entails that mutation and selection are unguided, unplanned, and unintended.
charity.decisiveQualification: Plantinga distinguishes scientific randomness from metaphysical absence of guidance and acknowledges that naturalism conjoined with evolution excludes divine design.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The modal route is stable: a scientifically random mutation can still be intentionally caused, so the scientific mechanism does not logically exclude guidance.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Definitions from Mayr and Sober directly support the limited randomness claim, but the proposed divine orchestration remains a possibility rather than evidence of actuality.

responsiveness.rationale: As an opening constructive it clearly addresses the stated compatibility question and anticipates the randomness objection.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The move directly advances the central compatibility bridge.

representationalCharity.rationale: It presents the unguided interpretation in recognizable form and preserves the distinction between evolution alone and evolution conjoined with naturalism.

proMoves.evidenceBasis: Events 202–338 contain the clearest combined statement of divine orchestration, the technical meaning of random mutation, and the distinction between evolutionary theory and a naturalistic gloss.

conMoves.speaker: Daniel Dennett
conMoves.proposition: Evolutionary theory cannot demonstrate the absence of intelligent intervention, but this bare compatibility leaves divine guidance evidentially gratuitous and unsupported.

sourceSpan.excerpt: I agree with Alvin that contemporary evolutionary theory can't demonstrate the absence of intelligent design... There's not a shred of evidence for any such fantasy.

conMoves.attributionBasis: The span occurs in Dennett's formally introduced response and uses first-person reference to Plantinga's case.

components.text: Concedes that evolutionary theory does not demonstrate the absence of intelligent design and is consistent with intervention.
Argues that logical compatibility supplies no evidence that divine intervention occurred.

response.rationale: Dennett accepts the modal conclusion and directly contests its evidential significance, contacting both indispensable components of the selected compatibility case.

precisionFindings.rationale: The distinction between consistency and evidential support is explicit, though the word 'fantasy' is rhetorically loaded.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Dennett carefully concedes possibility but asserts total evidential absence without surveying every theistic warrant offered in the debate.

charity.alternative: Plantinga's claim is only that divine guidance is compatible with Darwinism, not that evolutionary science proves divine intervention.
charity.decisiveQualification: Dennett expressly concedes the limited compatibility claim before arguing that it lacks evidential force.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The compatibility/evidence distinction is explicit and the concession fits the subsequent criticism.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The demand for positive evidence is appropriate, but the categorical claim that there is not a shred of evidence is asserted more broadly than this span documents.

responsiveness.rationale: The reply explicitly concedes the modal point and targets the decisive gap between possibility and evidential support.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It materially advances the con route's central evidential-insufficiency bridge.

representationalCharity.rationale: Despite dismissive terminology, Dennett accurately preserves Plantinga's limited compatibility thesis before criticizing its significance.

conMoves.evidenceBasis: Events 1437–1470 contain Dennett's express concession and the immediate evidential challenge; later Superman illustrations develop rather than replace this proposition.

sections.title: Cellular complexity and Behe's evidential case
sections.rationale: The parties directly contest whether cellular complexity and Behe's work provide empirical reason to prefer guided evolution.

proMoves.speaker: Alvin Plantinga
proMoves.proposition: Behe's quantitative argument from malaria, mutation, and protein-machine complexity makes unguided selection's production of the cell improbable, though the case is far from conclusive.

sourceSpan.excerpt: His argument is one of the few serious and quantitative arguments in this area... the argument seems reasonably powerful, though very far from conclusive.

proMoves.attributionBasis: The span is part of Plantinga's uninterrupted opening address.

response.rationale: This is the selected constructive presentation of the subsidiary design-evidence bridge.

precisionFindings.rationale: Plantinga identifies the source, empirical subject, probabilistic conclusion, and his lay status while stating that the argument is far from conclusive.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The stated force is deliberately modest and repeatedly qualified by Plantinga's lack of expertise and the argument's inconclusiveness.

charity.alternative: Unguided selection can produce complex cellular machinery and apparent gaps reflect incomplete young science rather than design.
charity.decisiveQualification: Plantinga presents Behe's claim as probabilistic and explicitly far from conclusive rather than as a demonstrated failure of evolution.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The conditional inference from an allegedly low unguided likelihood to comparative support for theism is intelligible, but rival guided and naturalistic likelihoods remain underdeveloped.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The move names an empirical case but does not present its quantitative premises or engage the scientific rebuttals needed to carry the conclusion.

responsiveness.rationale: As a constructive it advances a relevant subsidiary evidential route but expressly cannot outline the underlying argument.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It supports the declared subsidiary design-evidence bridge.

representationalCharity.rationale: The unguided alternative is stated without caricature and the conclusion is carefully limited, though its existing responses are not canvassed.

proMoves.evidenceBasis: Events 438–459 are the strongest concise presentation; later cellular-complexity discussion repeats and expands the same conditional evidential claim.

conMoves.speaker: Daniel Dennett
conMoves.proposition: If Behe were nearly right, scientists would have strong incentives to demonstrate irreducible complexity; their failure to pursue or confirm it, together with acknowledged knowledge gaps, makes Behe's success improbable rather than evidentially supportive.

sourceSpan.excerpt: If Behe is right or anywhere near right, why aren't there hordes of evolutionary biologists and biochemists... So... the probability that Behe is right or anywhere near right is negligible.

conMoves.attributionBasis: The span is within Dennett's uninterrupted response presentation.

components.text: Challenges Behe's evidential credibility by predicting conspicuous scientific pursuit and confirmation if the claim were nearly right.
Distinguishes acknowledged gaps in young microbiology from positive evidence of irreducible complexity.

response.rationale: Dennett diagnoses a failed empirical prediction of the Behe hypothesis and explicitly concludes that Behe's being right is negligible.

precisionFindings.rationale: The argument is recoverable, but 'scientists rush to their labs' imperfectly specifies the relevant scientific population and incentives.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Career incentives and absence of a rush are relevant but do not alone warrant the stated negligible probability, especially when Dennett acknowledges difficult open problems.

charity.alternative: Behe offers a quantitative but explicitly inconclusive argument that unresolved cellular complexity favors guidance.
charity.decisiveQualification: Dennett recognizes that real gaps remain, but argues they are not positive evidence of irreducible complexity.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The incentive-based modus tollens is intelligible, but it depends on a contestable prediction about research behavior and rewards.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Scientific incentives and acknowledged gaps are relevant evidence, yet no representative review findings or direct technical refutation are developed within the selected span.

responsiveness.rationale: The reply directly attacks the evidential warrant and states the defeating consequence for Plantinga's conditional reliance on Behe.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It supports the con route's subsidiary Behe-rebuttal bridge.

representationalCharity.rationale: Dennett reproduces Plantinga's conditional accurately and acknowledges genuine gaps, although his rhetoric sharpens the conclusion beyond Plantinga's modest formulation.

conMoves.evidenceBasis: Events 1841–1904 contain the complete probabilistic counterargument and the qualification that cellular evolutionary histories include genuine gaps.

sections.title: Methodological practice and metaphysical naturalism
sections.rationale: A distinct exchange contests whether reputable inquiry assumes metaphysical naturalism or merely uses methods compatible with theistic practitioners.

proMoves.speaker: Alvin Plantinga
proMoves.proposition: Scientific practice does not assume that God does not exist; theistic physicists can investigate how a divinely created world works without producing hypotheses that entail God.

sourceSpan.excerpt: If he's using the word naturalism the way I defined it... in physics... it's not assumed that there is no such person as God.

proMoves.attributionBasis: The moderator has returned the floor to Plantinga, who explicitly attributes and answers Dennett's claim.

components.text: Uses Dennett's statement against Plantinga's explicit definition of naturalism as denial of God.
Offers theistic physicists as a counterexample to the claim that scientific investigation assumes God's nonexistence.

response.rationale: Plantinga diagnoses an equivocation between metaphysical naturalism and methodological practice and explicitly concludes that Dennett's claim is false under the stipulated definition.

precisionFindings.rationale: The move explicitly fixes the disputed definition and distinguishes failure to entail God from assuming God's nonexistence.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The counterexample defeats the universal wording under Plantinga's definition, though it does not fully settle what procedural assumptions govern scientific explanations.

charity.alternative: Reputable inquiry procedurally excludes supernatural intentions when assessing empirical explanations.
charity.decisiveQualification: Plantinga answers the literal metaphysical definition Dennett used, while distinguishing it from scientists declining to derive God in their hypotheses.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The definitional distinction and counterexample coherently defeat the universal claim if 'naturalism' means denial of God.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The existence and practice of theistic physicists is a pertinent counterexample, though the institutional norms of explanation are not independently documented.

responsiveness.rationale: The move directly identifies the equivocation, supplies a counterexample, and states why the original universal claim fails.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It supports the pro route's subsidiary methodological-distinction bridge.

representationalCharity.rationale: It quotes the substance of Dennett's claim and tests it under the previously declared definition, while acknowledging a nearby methodological interpretation.

proMoves.evidenceBasis: Events 2285–2307 are Plantinga's direct reply to Dennett's universal assertion about courts and scientific investigation.

conMoves.speaker: Daniel Dennett
conMoves.proposition: Naturalistic explanation is tacitly assumed in reputable courts and scientific investigation, as illustrated by preferring an evidenced natural causal account over an ungrounded intentional-intervention possibility.

sourceSpan.excerpt: In all likelihood... Fred's death was by natural causes... naturalism however is passively assumed in all reputable courts of law and throughout scientific investigation.

conMoves.attributionBasis: The span is within Dennett's uninterrupted formal response and develops his own courtroom analogy.

components.text: The target's decisive component is that scientific mechanisms do not logically exclude divine guidance.

response.rationale: The analogy supplies contrary material about evidential practice but does not dispute Plantinga's modal compatibility component; it instead argues that practice defaults to natural causes.

precisionFindings.rationale: The move shifts between methodological preference for natural causes and Plantinga's metaphysical definition of naturalism, while universalizing across all reputable courts and science.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The courtroom illustration supports a methodological default but not the unqualified universal claim that metaphysical naturalism is assumed everywhere.

charity.alternative: Scientific practice can restrict itself to natural mechanisms without assuming the metaphysical proposition that God does not exist.
charity.decisiveQualification: Plantinga defines naturalism metaphysically, whereas Dennett's strongest illustration establishes an evidential or methodological norm.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The analogy supports preferring evidenced natural causes, but the conclusion equivocates between methodological and metaphysical naturalism.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The evidential structure of the courtroom case is concrete and relevant, though it cannot establish the sweeping institutional generalization.

responsiveness.rationale: It provides issue-bearing contrary material about explanatory standards without contacting the target's logical-compatibility component.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly advances the central con bridge concerning naturalistic method.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move does not preserve Plantinga's decisive distinction between metaphysical naturalism and methodological restriction, and that omission affects the inference.

conMoves.evidenceBasis: Events 1700–1754 contain the natural-cause analogy, the concession that naturalism was not independently established, and the universal claim about reputable inquiry.

sections.title: Evolution, truth tracking, and the self-defeat argument
sections.rationale: The largest section covers the debate's most sustained decisive exchange: whether naturalism and evolution make reliable cognition improbable and thereby become self-defeating.

proMoves.speaker: Alvin Plantinga
proMoves.proposition: If naturalism and evolution make reliable cognition improbable, accepting them supplies an undefeated defeater for cognitive reliability and consequently for naturalism and evolution themselves.

sourceSpan.excerpt: The probability of R on N and E is low... N and E is self-defeating and hence can't rationally be accepted... natural selection doesn't give a fig about true belief just as such.

proMoves.attributionBasis: The span is part of Plantinga's uninterrupted opening presentation and explicitly labels the argument's premises.

response.rationale: This is the opening selected statement of the full naturalism-and-evolution self-defeat route.

precisionFindings.rationale: N, E, and R are defined, the conclusion is rational self-defeat rather than falsity, and the materialist variants are introduced explicitly.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The propagation from an undefeated reliability defeater is structured, but the premise assigning roughly one-half truth probability to beliefs is not established merely by selection's direct focus on behavior.

charity.alternative: Adaptive neurophysiology can causally realize truth-sensitive content, allowing selection for successful behavior to indirectly favor reliable belief.
charity.decisiveQualification: Plantinga considers reductive and nonreductive materialism but treats truth and adaptivity as insufficiently linked in each.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The defeater propagation is coherent conditional on the low-probability premise, but the route from selection for behavior to a one-half truth probability contains a material unsupported bridge.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The argument supplies explicit models and a numerical illustration, yet independence and the alleged disconnect between adaptive content and truth are asserted rather than empirically or semantically defended.

responsiveness.rationale: As the central constructive, it directly addresses the motion's cognition-under-naturalism question and states the claimed consequence.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It supports the complete pro motion bridge by connecting evolutionary naturalism to rational self-defeat.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move addresses several materialist accounts, but it underrepresents the strongest causal or teleosemantic link between adaptive success and true content.

proMoves.evidenceBasis: Events 970–1098 state the full defeater chain and begin the decisive defense of its low-probability premise; subsequent variants repeat the same truth/adaptivity separation.

proMoves.speaker: Alvin Plantinga
proMoves.proposition: Dennett's examples show that actual cognition can be corrected, but they do not answer the conditional probability argument; calculators track truth because intelligent designers made them do so, which does not establish truth tracking under unguided evolution.

sourceSpan.excerpt: That isn't the question. The question is rather... the probability that our faculties could be reliable... Calculators... track the truth... because they've been designed to do that by us.

proMoves.attributionBasis: The span occurs in Plantinga's moderator-authorized reply and explicitly addresses Dennett by name.

components.text: Distinguishes evidence that cognition is corrigible and actually tracks truth from the conditional probability of reliability given naturalism and evolution.
Does not fully answer Dennett's proposed evolutionary and cultural mechanisms linking adaptive systems to truth tracking.

response.rationale: Plantinga exposes a relevant conditional/actual distinction and challenges the calculator analogy, but leaves Dennett's selection-and-correction mechanism only partly answered.

precisionFindings.rationale: The move clearly distinguishes actual reliability from its conditional probability and identifies the limited role of the calculator analogy.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The objection successfully identifies what evidence must address, but treating Dennett as merely announcing reliability overlooks his selection and correction mechanisms.

charity.alternative: Evolution produces truth-tracking syntactic systems, and cultural-scientific bootstrapping corrects their defects.
charity.decisiveQualification: Plantinga recognizes Dennett's calculator analogy but emphasizes that human calculators are intentionally designed and therefore do not independently model unguided origins.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The distinction between actual reliability and conditional probability is valid, and the calculator objection is coherent, though it does not defeat the broader evolutionary mechanism.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The reply rests mainly on conceptual distinctions rather than external evidence, but those distinctions directly test the inference Dennett offered.

responsiveness.rationale: It contacts the decisive conditional-probability issue but does not fully engage selection, cultural correction, and causal truth-tracking as a combined answer.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly defends the pro route's central reliability-defeater bridge.

representationalCharity.rationale: It accurately presents the calculator point but compresses Dennett's broader argument into an announcement that cognition tracks truth.

proMoves.evidenceBasis: Events 2335–2398 contain Plantinga's direct conditional-probability distinction and his developed reply to the calculator analogy.

conMoves.speaker: Daniel Dennett
conMoves.proposition: The low-reliability premise is false because evolved systems can be reverse-engineered and tested for acuity, selection disfavors low-reliability cognitive devices, and science systematically corrects cognitive shortcomings.

sourceSpan.excerpt: The probability... is low. I think this is just plain false... Science is a systematic effort to remove the cognitive shortcomings... evolution can design... syntactic engines that track truth systematically.

conMoves.attributionBasis: The span is within Dennett's uninterrupted formal response and expressly quotes the first premise.

components.text: Rejects the decisive premise that reliable cognition is improbable under naturalism and evolution by proposing selection for truth-tracking syntactic systems.
Blocks the downstream self-defeat conclusion by arguing that reliability can be measured, corrected, and enhanced without divine assurance.

response.rationale: Dennett directly attacks the first premise and explains why its failure prevents the claimed reliability defeater.

precisionFindings.rationale: The truth-tracking and correction route is clear, though it moves between animal sense-organ reliability, human propositional cognition, and culturally enhanced science.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The examples strongly establish corrigibility and some reliability, but do not by themselves quantify the probability of broad propositional reliability under the full naturalist model.

charity.alternative: Selection directly rewards adaptive physiology and behavior, leaving the truth of associated belief content probabilistically unconstrained.
charity.decisiveQualification: Dennett directly addresses the low-probability premise by proposing indirect selection for systems that reliably track environmental truths.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The route from adaptive performance to truth-sensitive mechanisms and from error detection to improved reliability is coherent, with a remaining bridge from sensory success to general belief reliability.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Reverse engineering, measured acuity, prosthetic correction, and scientific bias controls are concrete supporting practices, though the broad semantic conclusion remains partly extrapolated.

responsiveness.rationale: The reply identifies and attacks the decisive first premise and explains how evolved cognition can be reliable without divine support.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It attacks the pro route's central reliability-defeater bridge.

representationalCharity.rationale: Dennett states the low-probability premise accurately and addresses its naturalistic setting rather than substituting a different conclusion.

conMoves.evidenceBasis: Events 1970–2026 provide the strongest compact version of Dennett's reverse-engineering, correction, syntactic-engine, and selection reply.

conMoves.speaker: Daniel Dennett
conMoves.proposition: Cognitive systems can be causally organized so that truth tracking is required for their persistence; evolutionary biology and cognitive science support such designs, just as wings aid survival by flying well.

sourceSpan.excerpt: Evolution has created these things where there is indeed causal relation between truth and those states... that it persists in tracking truth is a precondition for its continuing in the system.

conMoves.attributionBasis: The transcript explicitly marks Dennett entering after Plantinga's answer, and he speaks in the first person about his long-standing argument.

components.text: Supplies the missing causal mechanism by which evolution can make truth tracking a condition of a cognitive state's persistence.
Argues that evolvability of designed truth-tracking systems, not merely human manufacture of calculators, is the relevant analogy.

response.rationale: Dennett directly answers Plantinga's demand for a link between adaptive causation and true content, and explains why intelligent human manufacture is not essential to the analogy.

precisionFindings.rationale: The causal truth-tracking thesis is recoverable, but the scope and operation of mechanisms that disassemble non-tracking states remain compressed.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The possibility and adaptive rationale are strong, but the claim that all relevant cognitive systems evolved this way outruns the detailed support supplied in the span.

charity.alternative: Adaptive neurophysiology can generate false belief content without reducing behavioral fitness, so causal connection alone does not make content true.
charity.decisiveQualification: Dennett answers that persistent cognitive states are selected within systems whose functioning depends specifically on continued truth tracking.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The wings analogy clearly identifies an intermediate functional bridge: cognition aids survival through accurate representation, not independently of it.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The mechanism is plausible and tied to cognitive science and evolutionary biology, but the empirical generalization and disassembly processes are asserted rather than demonstrated in detail.

responsiveness.rationale: The reply directly supplies the causal truth-to-fitness connection Plantinga said was missing and contacts both selected components.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly advances the con route's central truth-tracking bridge.

representationalCharity.rationale: Dennett engages Plantinga's strongest separation between adaptive causation and true content and identifies the qualification he believes closes that gap.

conMoves.evidenceBasis: Events 2650–2713 contain Dennett's strongest later development: causal dependence, removal of non-tracking states, evolutionary design, and the wings analogy.

pro.rationale: No distinct debate-wide consequence remains outside the selected moves, response links, importance values, and section weights; compatibility and self-defeat are already directly represented and rated.

eligibility.completionCriterion: The pro route must establish both compatibility and the rational self-defeat of naturalism plus evolution.
eligibility.distinctConsequence: None beyond consequences already captured in the selected motion-level and central moves.
eligibility.counterfactual: Removing the adjustment leaves every pro burden consequence represented by selected moves and their ratings.

con.rationale: No distinct debate-wide consequence remains uncaptured; evidential insufficiency, methodology, Behe, and truth tracking are represented in selected moves and response structures.

eligibility.completionCriterion: The con route must show that bare compatibility lacks evidential force and that evolved cognition can rationally track truth.
eligibility.distinctConsequence: None beyond consequences already captured in the selected replies, burden contacts, and section weights.
eligibility.counterfactual: Removing the adjustment leaves every con burden consequence represented by selected moves and their ratings.
